title: UE slice-1 side-by-side reference frame is absent from the committed PR surface (gitignored, broken links)
evidence: frames/.gitignore: "ue-*.png". PR body line 16: "UE slice-1 reference (the bar, read-only): `frames/ue-slice1-2-drawn-pipe.png`, `frames/ue-slice1-3-packet.png`." gallery.html section 4: "". Worktree ls of frames/: no ue-* files exist. The committed side-by-side (2564x720 = two 1280px own-build frames) caption: "LEFT: v2 at HEAD (before) · RIGHT: the polish pass. One image, one seed — only the look changed."
detail: Briefing deliverable requires 'plus one side-by-side vs a UE slice-1 reference frame' in the PR body. UE frames are gitignored and absent, so reviewers see broken images and no UE comparison exists in-repo.
recommended_fix: Copy the two UE reference frames into frames/ (they are the project's own prior art, or use the documented read-only path) and add a true UE-vs-after side-by-side image; drop the .gitignore rule.

title: Sprite/asset regeneration contradicts the frozen spec's explicit Never ('the committed sprite pipeline is untouched')
evidence: spec-v2-look-polish.md:35: "**Never:** No gameplay/canon-surface changes, no catalog edits, no LOG_VERSION bump, no serialization change, no sprite/asset regeneration (the committed sprite pipeline is untouched), no new node types...". gen_sprites.py diff: "+    add_outline(name + \"_o\", bw, bd, 0.09, 1.20)  # roof overhang 1.14x + 0.06" and "+    add_cube(name + \"_walls\", (0, 0, 0.125), (bw, bd, 0.07), mat_hex(name + \"_body\", body_hex, shade=0.80))". git diff 3a26217..HEAD --name-only -- assets/: 11 sprite PNGs + sprites.json regenerated. spec's "## Spec Change Log" (line 85) is empty.
detail: The frozen-after-approval spec forbids sprite regeneration; the PR attributes it to user gate-r1 feedback, but the spec was never renegotiated in-repo and its change log records nothing.
recommended_fix: Record the gate-r1 renegotiation in the spec's Spec Change Log (what changed, who approved, when) so the frozen Never and the shipped code stop contradicting each other.

title: Stream-triangle glint contradicts the frozen spec's I/O matrix ('no glint on triangles')
evidence: spec-v2-look-polish.md:44: "| PACKET GLINT | non-circle shapes (triangle/…, unknown classes) | glint only on circles (the fallback dot path) — shapes keep their current look | no glint on triangles |". view.odin:1079-1083: "// 8.x the stream glint (v2-look-polish, user gate): the streaming / // triangles get the SAME warm-cream highlight as the circular dots ... rl.DrawCircleV({pos.x - r * 0.16, pos.y - r * 0.34}, r * 0.20, rl.Color{250, 246, 238, body.a})". detail: Frozen matrix says triangles keep their current look; the code glints them. PR documents user gate-r1 approval ('the stream might need the same touch up') but the spec was never amended.

title: LEFOU pass mutes pipe tiers/water/park and halves grid blend far beyond the spec's single sanctioned canvas-token change; 'tier colors stay load-bearing' weakened
evidence: spec-v2-look-polish.md:68: "- [ ] `data/palette.json` + `app/render/palette.odin` -- lift the canvas token to the new warm-cream (~#EDE2C8; all three copies: json, fallback_palette, jcol default) -- the palette step." spec:35: "no pipe-color meaning change (tier colors stay load-bearing ...)". data/palette.json diff: "\"pipe_copper\":   [150, 142, 132, 255]," (was [142,94,46]). view.odin:213: "u8((u16(g.r)*9 + u16(c.r)*91) / 100)," (grid 18→9). Rec.601 luminance: new copper 143.3 vs new steel 133.0 (~10 apart; old copper 102.9 vs steel 133.0, ~30 apart + strong copper hue). Spec Change Log empty; amendment 9's authority is an out-of-repo 'Gru relay'.
detail: Frozen spec sanctioned one palette token (canvas) and declared tier colors load-bearing; copper/steel now differ by ~10 luma and near-identical gray hue, shifting tier identity onto width/stripes. Relies on unverifiable user approval.
recommended_fix: Add a Spec Change Log entry citing the user's full-repolish ruling; flag the copper/steel convergence (~10 luma) explicitly at the lavish gate so the human judges tier readability.
